periods.narrative: Diplomatic momentum consolidated around trilateral talks set for on/after November 10, with all sides confirming 'in principle' while hardening preconditions. Russia continued offensive operations (337 drones launched; no ceasefire yet), the EU pressed to keep sanctions on, and Iran reiterated demands for prior relief while Israel rejected any enrichment-preserving deal. Markets barely moved: talk of talks does not change fundamentals within a week.

periods.narrative: Talks converged procedurally: all parties confirmed attendance at the 10 November trilateral technical talks, but substantive gaps widened — Kyiv demands guarantees-first sequencing, Moscow demands relief-first sequencing, and neither side blinked. Iran showed a modest moderation: Pezeshkian's parallel-talks offer and the US willingness to discuss sequenced relief created a narrow diplomatic channel despite Khamenei's hardline framing and Netanyahu's rejectionism. Markets and institutions reacted modestly; high-frequency war indicators were largely flat.
